content: Acriflavine is a topical antiseptic that is available in the form of an orange or brown powder. It can be harmful if it comes into contact with the eyes or if it is inhaled. As a dye, it has the potential to stain the skin and may cause irritation upon contact. Commercial formulations of acriflavine are often combined with another compound, proflavine. This substance is marketed under various names. Acriflavine was first developed in 1912 by Paul Ehrlich, a German medical researcher, and it was utilized during the First World War as a treatment for sleeping sickness. The compound is chemically derived from acridine. The hydrochloride form of acriflavine is known to be more irritating than its base form. In addition to its use as a topical antiseptic, acriflavine is also employed in the treatment of external fungal infections in aquarium fish.
